New plan: I failed because I misinterpreted the emotional arc of the dialogue. Arthur repeatedly apologizes, admits fault, and offers to make amends, which strongly indicates **Remorseful** rather than just Defeated. While he feels defeated by the situation, his primary active emotion driving his actions (apologizing, trying to change) is remorse. I underestimated the intensity of Remorseful (giving it 5 instead of higher) and overestimated Defeated (giving it 8). I should have recognized that his persistent, sincere apologies and admission of guilt point to a high score for Remorseful, while his feeling of being unable to fix the past points to a moderate score for Defeated. I will re-evaluate the emotions based on the specific actions of apologizing and admitting fault.
